question: An organisation reports that a Copilot feature described in Microsoft's documentation does not appear anywhere in its Sales environment. What should you check first?
options: Whether the feature is included in the Sales plan they hold
Whether the feature has been enabled in the environment's app settings
Whether users have been assigned the correct security roles
Whether the environment is in a supported region
explanation: Sales Premium and Sales Enterprise differ in which AI capabilities are included, so a feature can be absent rather than misconfigured. Debugging configuration for something the plan does not carry is the expensive misdiagnosis.

question: A seller's emails are not appearing in Dynamics. Their mailbox record shows the mailbox configured for server-side synchronisation. What is most likely missing?
options: The mailbox has not been approved by an administrator
The seller has not installed Dynamics 365 App for Outlook
The seller lacks a Sales licence
The timeline is filtered to exclude email
explanation: Approval is a distinct administrative step before test and enable, and an unapproved mailbox simply does not sync. The failure is reported on the mailbox record rather than to the user, which is why it goes unnoticed.

question: Copilot record summaries are consistently two lines long for one region's opportunities and detailed for another's. What is the most likely cause?
options: That region's activity is not being tracked into Dataverse
The summarisation feature is disabled for that region's business unit
That region's users hold a lower Sales plan
The summary length setting differs per team
explanation: Summarisation reads the record and its related activities, so a thin timeline summarises thinly. The cause sits two layers below the symptom, in mailbox synchronisation and tracking habits.

question: A sales manager wants the business process flow to prevent an opportunity reaching Propose before a budget field is filled. What should you tell them?
options: A business process flow guides but does not enforce; enforcement needs other logic
Set the stage's required fields and the flow will block progression everywhere
Scope the process flow to the table so it runs server-side
Add a business rule to the flow's stage with a validation action
explanation: A business process flow is guidance and visibility. Records can still be written out of order by a cloud flow, an import, or the API, so any real enforcement has to sit on the data rather than on the process bar.

question: Before a bulk load of 40,000 leads, which configuration matters most for the AI features that will run afterwards?
options: Duplicate detection rules
Timeline filtering on the lead form
Currency and exchange rate configuration
The lead form's business process flow
explanation: A duplicated estate degrades scoring, routing, and every agent that reasons over the records, and it is far cheaper to prevent than to clean afterwards.

question: A regional manager must see their own records and those of the sellers reporting to them, and no others. Which privilege depth achieves this?
options: Parent-Child Business Unit
User
Business Unit
Organisation
explanation: Parent-Child extends the manager's view down the business unit hierarchy. User would give only their own records and Business Unit would stop at their own unit without including its children.

question: An agent summarises accounts for whichever seller asks. What is the risk of configuring it with an elevated service identity?
options: It will summarise records the requesting seller has no right to see
It will be unable to write activity back to the record
It will consume capacity against the service account's allocation only
It will bypass duplicate detection when creating records
explanation: An agent acting on a seller's behalf should see what that seller sees. An elevated identity produces summaries containing data the requester was never entitled to, which is a leak that presents as a working feature.

question: A product is being withdrawn from sale but appears on two years of closed opportunities. What should you do?
options: Retire the product
Delete the product
Remove it from every price list
Set its quantity on hand to zero
explanation: Retiring stops the product being added to new records while leaving it on historical ones. Deleting would damage the history, and removing it from price lists leaves it active and addable.

question: Analysis of revenue by product is impossible because most opportunity lines are write-in products. What does this indicate?
options: The catalogue does not match what the organisation actually sells
The price lists are missing a currency
Opportunity revenue is set to system-calculated
The products are retired rather than active
explanation: A write-in product carries no product id, so revenue against it cannot be analysed by product. Heavy reliance on write-ins is a symptom of a catalogue that does not cover the real portfolio.

question: Which two must exist before a product can be given a price? Choose two.
options: A unit group with a base unit
A price list with a currency
An active business process flow on the product table
A product family containing the product
explanation: A unit group and base unit come first, then a price list item ties the product to a currency and a price. Product families group products and carry inheritable properties but are not required for pricing.

question: Match each data movement option to the case it suits.

pairs.definition: A one-off load with column mapping and duplicate detection
Repeated ingestion on a schedule from a source system
Taking a working copy out for offline analysis or bulk edit

explanation: The four differ by frequency and direction. Choosing a one-off import for what is really a recurring feed is how an estate drifts out of step with its source system.

question: Which requirement is best served by an agent rather than a Copilot feature?
options: Researching new leads overnight and preparing briefings before sellers log in
Drafting a reply to an email the seller has open
Summarising an opportunity record the seller is reading
Generating a meeting recap after a call the seller attended
explanation: Copilot features assist a seller who is present; agents act without one. Work that must happen when nobody is at the keyboard is the defining case for an agent.

question: A team proposes a custom Deal table alongside Opportunity to hold their own fields. Why should you object?
options: First-party AI features understand the standard model and would ignore it
Custom tables cannot hold lookups to Account
Custom tables are excluded from Dataverse security
Custom tables cannot appear in a model-driven app
explanation: Scoring, forecasting, the agents, and Copilot summarisation all read the standard tables. A parallel custom table is invisible to every one of them, which is why extending Opportunity is the correct move.

question: A sales director wants a cross-system analysis of win rates against marketing spend. Where does this belong?
options: A Power BI report embedded into Sales
A Sales dashboard built on views
A model-driven chart on the opportunity table
A goal metric with a rollup query
explanation: Analytical questions spanning volume and other systems are Power BI's job, embedded rather than reimplemented. Sales dashboards and charts answer operational questions against live records.

question: An agent pilot against 200 leads cost very little. Rolling it out across 20,000 leads exhausted the monthly allocation in a week. Why?
options: Agent capacity is consumed per action, so it scales with record volume
Capacity is charged per user once an agent is enabled
Pilot environments do not consume production capacity
The agent switched to a more expensive model at scale
explanation: Consumption is proportional to the records the agent touches rather than to headcount, so capacity planning is an exercise in estimating volume. A pilot's cost does not extrapolate by user count.

question: Which agent capability most clearly warrants human review before it is made autonomous?
options: Emailing prospects on the organisation's behalf
Summarising an account's recent activity
Ranking leads for a seller's work list
Drafting internal notes on an opportunity
explanation: Contacting customers is an outward-facing, hard-to-reverse action taken in the organisation's name. The other three produce internal output a human reads before anything leaves the building.

question: A specific assignment rule for enterprise leads never fires, although matching leads exist. What should you check?
options: Whether a broader rule sits above it in the evaluation order
Whether the sellers have capacity configured
Whether the leads have a predictive score
Whether the rule's business unit matches the leads' owner
explanation: Assignment rules are evaluated in order, so a broad rule placed above a specific one absorbs everything and the specific rule is unreachable. Ordering is the first thing to inspect.

question: What does a sequence in the Sales accelerator provide?
options: A defined cadence of steps surfaced to the seller as the next action due
A rule that routes records to the right seller
A model that scores leads by likelihood to qualify
A dashboard showing pipeline by stage
explanation: A sequence attaches a methodology to a record and the work list surfaces the next step, so the cadence becomes the interface rather than something a seller must remember.

question: Conversational intelligence shows no insights at all after deployment. What is the most likely cause?
options: Calls are not being recorded through a supported channel
The predictive scoring model has not been trained
Sellers lack the Sales accelerator work list
The opportunity forecast has not been configured
explanation: Conversational intelligence analyses recorded calls, so no recordings means no analysis. Recording, consent, and channel support are the prerequisites to check before configuration.

question: Relationship health scores are blank for most accounts. What is the underlying cause?
options: Interaction history is not being synchronised or tracked
The accounts lack a primary contact
Relationship intelligence requires a Power BI licence
The accounts are owned by teams rather than users
explanation: Relationship intelligence computes health and who-knows-whom from interaction history. With no synchronised, tracked activity there is nothing to compute from.

question: A regional manager adjusts a forecast figure upward. What happens to the rolled-up value?
options: It is retained, with the adjustment recorded alongside it
It is overwritten by the adjusted figure
It is recalculated to match the adjustment
It is locked until the forecast period closes
explanation: Adjustments sit alongside the rolled-up numbers rather than replacing them, which keeps a manager's judgement visible and auditable against what the pipeline actually said.

question: A seller complains that a lead's predictive score did not change after they updated several fields. What should you explain?
options: Scores are refreshed on a schedule rather than recalculated on edit
The fields they edited are excluded from the model by design
Scores only update when the lead's owner changes
The model must be retrained manually after every edit
explanation: Scoring runs on a schedule and models retrain periodically, so a score is a recent estimate that ranks a queue rather than a live judgement of one record.

question: Which two prerequisites must be in place before deploying agents in Sales? Choose two.
options: Capacity or credits provisioned for agent consumption
The underlying record data the agents will reason over
A Power BI workspace for agent telemetry
A separate environment dedicated to agents
explanation: Agents consume provisioned capacity and reason over the Dataverse estate, so both must exist. Neither a Power BI workspace nor a dedicated environment is required.

question: Put these steps in order for making agent-generated work actionable for sellers.
items: Ensure the record data the agent reasons over is complete
Provision capacity for the agent's expected volume
Configure work assignment so agent output is routed to a seller
Configure the accelerator work list so the next action is surfaced
explanation: Data comes before capacity because an agent reasoning over poor data wastes whatever it is given. Routing then assignment ordering matters because agent output without prioritisation arrives as an undifferentiated pile.

question: An organisation is planning predictive opportunity scoring. Judge each statement.

statements.text: The model needs closed history containing both wins and losses.
A field only populated after a deal closes should be excluded from the model.
Excluding a leaking field can lower reported accuracy while improving real predictive value.
Scores are recalculated immediately whenever a contributing field changes.

explanation: Target leakage produces a model with excellent reported accuracy and no predictive value, because it is reading the answer. Scores refresh on a schedule, which is why sellers who expect live movement come to distrust them.

question: Why should leads that go nowhere be disqualified with a reason rather than deleted?
options: Disqualified leads with reasons are training data for predictive scoring
Deleted leads cannot be recreated with the same email address
Disqualification is required before an account can be created
Deleting a lead removes its associated account and contact
explanation: A model learns from both outcomes. Deleting the negatives leaves the model with only successes to learn from, which is how it concludes almost everything succeeds.

question: Sellers record budget, authority, need, and timeline in the lead's notes field. What should you change?
options: Capture each as a structured column so scoring, routing, and agents can read it
Add a business rule that requires the notes field to be filled
Move the notes to the timeline as a post
Add the notes field to the quick find view
explanation: Information in free text is invisible to scoring, routing, and every agent. The same content as structured fields becomes data all three can reason over.

question: A predictive lead scoring model reports 96 per cent accuracy but its scores do not distinguish leads that go on to qualify. What is the most likely cause?
options: Target leakage from a field populated only after the outcome is known
Too few attributes were included in the model
The model was trained on too much history
The scores are being refreshed too frequently
explanation: A leaking field lets the model read the answer, which produces a high reported score and no predictive value. Removing it usually lowers the reported number and raises the real one.

question: In which mode does the Sales Qualification Agent gather and summarise without contacting the prospect?
options: Research-only
Research and engage
Monitor-only
Assisted qualification
explanation: Research-only leaves every outbound contact to a human and produces a briefing that shortens the seller's preparation. Research and engage additionally lets the agent conduct an initial exchange.

question: Who should decide whether the Sales Qualification Agent runs in Research and engage mode?
options: The stakeholders who own brand and compliance
The Dataverse system administrator
The sellers whose leads it will work
The implementation partner configuring the agent
explanation: Engage mode means an autonomous system corresponds with prospects in the organisation's name, which makes it a brand and compliance decision rather than a technical one.

question: A seller disputes the Sales Qualification Agent's decision to deprioritise a lead. What allows the disagreement to be resolved?
options: The trail recording what the agent researched and why it concluded what it did
The lead's predictive score history
The agent's capacity consumption report
The sequence attached to the lead in the accelerator
explanation: The agent records its research and its reasoning, which turns a matter of opinion into something checkable. Without that trail the dispute cannot be settled on evidence.

question: What should be monitored on a deployed Sales Qualification Agent?
options: Whether its conclusions hold up against what sellers find, and its capacity consumption
Only its capacity consumption, since quality is subjective
Only the number of leads it processes each day
Only whether sellers open its briefings
explanation: Both halves matter: an agent that is cheap and wrong is worse than useless, and one that is right and unaffordable cannot be kept. Quality is measurable against seller outcomes.

question: When a lead is qualified, which records can Dynamics 365 Sales create?
options: An account, a contact, and an opportunity
An opportunity and a quote
A contact and an order
An account and a price list
explanation: Qualification converts interest into the records the rest of the process needs, and which of the three are created is configurable. Quotes and orders come later in the cycle.

question: Which two conditions must hold for predictive lead scoring to produce useful results? Choose two.
options: Enough closed history to learn from
Both qualified and disqualified outcomes represented
A business process flow applied to the lead table
Conversational intelligence enabled on the environment
explanation: Volume and both outcomes are what a model learns from. A process flow is presentation and conversational intelligence analyses calls; neither feeds lead scoring.

question: Put these steps in order for introducing the Sales Qualification Agent responsibly.
items: Confirm lead data quality and duplicate detection
Deploy the agent in Research-only mode
Compare the agent's conclusions against seller outcomes
Obtain brand and compliance sign-off before enabling engage mode
explanation: Data first, because an agent reasoning over a duplicated estate produces confident nonsense. Research-only establishes trust, measurement provides the evidence, and only then is customer contact a decision anybody can make responsibly.

question: Complete the statement about predictive scoring behaviour.

segments.text: A predictive lead score is refreshed

options: on a schedule, so it ranks a queue rather than judging a record live
whenever a contributing column is edited
only when the model is retrained

segments.text: , and fine-tuning the model chiefly means

options: choosing which attributes it may consider and excluding those that leak the outcome
adjusting the numeric threshold at which a lead counts as hot
increasing the volume of history it is trained on

explanation: Scheduled refresh is why a score does not move when a seller edits a field, and attribute selection — particularly removing fields that reveal the outcome — is what actually improves the model. Thresholds change reporting, not the model.

question: The Sales Opportunity Agent flags 80 per cent of the open pipeline every week and sellers have stopped reading its prompts. The 14-day threshold must not change. What should you do?
options: Approve the 38 outstanding mailboxes and establish tracking through Dynamics 365 App for Outlook
Restrict the agent to opportunities above a minimum value
Reduce how often the agent runs so fewer prompts are generated
Disable the agent until sellers ask for it to be re-enabled
explanation: "No activity for 14 days" is only true if activity is being recorded, and 38 of 60 sellers track nothing — the agent is reporting silence that is not real. Filtering or throttling reduces the volume of wrong prompts without making any of them right, which is why the threshold does not need to move.

question: The forecast and the regional reports differ by about 11 per cent. Which change reconciles them to a figure that follows the line items?
options: Set opportunity revenue to system-calculated so the total derives from opportunity products
Have regional managers report on the user-entered value instead
Add a rollup column on the opportunity summing its products
Rebuild the regional reports in Power BI against the same dataset
explanation: The two numbers diverge because the forecast reads a typed headline value while the regional reports sum the products. The requirement is a single figure that follows the line items, which is exactly what system-calculated revenue produces. A rollup would add a third number and recalculate on a schedule rather than on read.

question: The opportunity scoring model reports 94 per cent accuracy and scores nearly every open deal above 80. What must change, accepting that the reported accuracy will fall?
options: Close unsuccessful opportunities as lost instead of deleting them, then retrain
Retrain the model more frequently against the existing history
Raise the threshold at which a score counts as high
Exclude open opportunities from the training data
explanation: Brantwood deletes the deals that go nowhere, so the model has been trained almost entirely on wins and has correctly learned that everything succeeds. Retraining against the same one-sided history changes nothing, and moving the threshold relabels the output without making it informative.

question: Complete the assessment of the Sales Qualification Agent's contact with the regulated customer.

segments.text: The exchange happened because the agent was left in

options: Research and engage mode, which lets it correspond with prospects itself
Research-only mode, which permits automated follow-up email
monitor mode, which forwards prospect replies automatically

segments.text: , so to meet the requirement that no agent contacts a customer without named human authorisation you should

options: move it to Research-only and route its briefings to a seller who decides on contact
add the customer to a suppression list and leave the mode unchanged
reduce the agent's capacity so it sends fewer messages

explanation: Research-only is the mode in which every outbound contact stays with a human, which is what the requirement asks for across all customers rather than one. Suppressing a single customer leaves the same autonomous contact running against everyone else, and capacity limits how much it sends rather than whether it may.

question: Consider the Sales Research Agent briefing that led a seller to quote a corrected press article. Judge each statement.

statements.text: Findings drawn from Dynamics records and findings drawn from the public web should be distinguishable in the briefing.
Presenting both as one narrative invites a seller to repeat an unverified external claim as though it came from the account record.
External findings are only as reliable as the sources behind them and should be attributed.
Restricting the agent to internal records only would satisfy the requirement as stated.

explanation: The requirement is that a seller can tell which statements come from Brantwood's records and which come outside — that is a provenance requirement, not a request to remove external research. Removing external sources would satisfy it trivially by discarding the capability the agent was deployed for.

question: A price list is updated but several opportunity lines keep their old prices. Why?
options: Those lines have overridden prices and no longer follow the price list
The price list update has not been published
The opportunities are in a closed state
The products on those lines have been retired
explanation: Overriding a line's price detaches it from the price list, so subsequent list updates do not reach it. This is where reconciliation surprises come from.

question: Which Sales agent gathers information and produces a briefing without taking action on records?
options: The Sales Research Agent
The Sales Qualification Agent
The Sales Opportunity Agent
The Sales Close Agent
explanation: Research assembles and reports; qualification, opportunity, and close all act. That distinction is what decides which agent a requirement calls for.

question: What is the intended posture for the Sales Close Agent?
options: Collaboration, with the agent preparing and a named human deciding
Full autonomy, with review only when it escalates
Read-only analysis of closed deals
Scheduled batch processing outside working hours
explanation: The close is where money and commitments are, so its actions most need to be reviewable. The agent assembles and coordinates; the decision stays with a person.

question: How should the value of the Sales Close Agent be measured?
options: By whether its interventions shorten sales cycles
By how many actions it performs each week
By how much capacity it consumes
By how many opportunities it touches
explanation: An agent that generates activity without moving deals is measurable as such, and cycle time is the outcome it exists to change. Action counts measure effort rather than effect.

question: What does the research canvas add over a static briefing document?
options: A surface for exploring findings and following a thread
Automatic scheduling of follow-up activities
Enforcement of the opportunity's business process flow
Offline availability of the briefing in the mobile app
explanation: A wall of text nobody can interrogate has saved no time. The canvas exists so findings can be pursued rather than only read.

question: Which condition most limits the usefulness of the Sales Opportunity Agent?
options: Sellers not tracking email and meetings into Dataverse
Opportunities lacking a business process flow
The absence of a predictive opportunity score
Opportunity revenue being system-calculated
explanation: The agent reasons about what has and has not happened, and untracked activity looks identical to no activity. Deploying it before tracking habits exist is the standard way to make it useless.

question: Which setting keeps an opportunity's total honest against its line items?
options: System-calculated revenue
User-entered revenue
A rollup column over opportunity products
A business rule validating the total
explanation: System-calculated derives the total from the opportunity products on read. User-entered is the seller's negotiated number, chosen deliberately when the line items do not describe the deal.

question: A sales manager wants to work the pipeline as a board by stage with inline editing. What should you configure?
options: The opportunity pipeline view
An interactive dashboard on the opportunity table
A Power BI report embedded in the Sales app
A goal metric with a rollup query
explanation: The pipeline view is the board-by-stage surface with inline editing and aggregates. Dashboards and Power BI reports present information without being the working surface.

question: Which two are true of the Sales Close Agent? Choose two.
options: It leaves a trail of what it did and on what basis
It is intended to operate alongside a human decision-maker
It closes opportunities automatically once all products are priced
It replaces the opportunity business process flow
explanation: Its actions are reviewable and its posture is collaborative, because it works where money and commitments are. It neither closes deals unilaterally nor replaces the process flow.

question: Put these opportunity steps in the order the platform requires.
items: Ensure the product is active in the catalogue
Ensure a price list item exists for the product in the opportunity's currency
Add the product as an opportunity product
Apply a line-level discount if one has been negotiated
explanation: Only an active product can be added, and it needs a price in the opportunity's currency before it can be priced. Discounting is the last step and detaches the line from the price list.

question: Match each Sales agent to the work it does.

pairs.definition: Researches and, if configured, engages new leads
Watches open deals for stalls and missing next steps
Prepares and coordinates the work a close requires
Assembles a briefing from internal and external sources

explanation: The four map onto funnel position — top, middle, end — with research running alongside all three. Only the research agent takes no action on records.

question: A seller finds a record missing when working offline in the Sales mobile app. What is the most likely cause?
options: The record's table is not in the configured offline profile
The seller's licence does not cover mobile use
The record was created after the app was installed
Offline mode requires the record to be assigned to the seller
explanation: Which tables are available offline is a deliberate configuration. A table outside the profile simply is not there, and the seller discovers it at exactly the wrong moment.

question: Why does configuring Teams calling inside Sales matter for conversational intelligence?
options: Calling from a record logs the call, giving the analysis something to work from
Teams calling transcribes calls in place of conversational intelligence
It is a licensing prerequisite for the Sales accelerator
It replaces the need for server-side synchronisation
explanation: Conversational intelligence analyses captured calls, so a calling path that reliably logs against the record is what makes the data exist. It does not replace the analysis or the mailbox sync.

question: An organisation adds an SMS channel for seller outreach. Which requirement follows?
options: Consent and record-keeping must be configured, and messages logged on the timeline
Sellers must be licensed for Dynamics 365 Customer Insights
SMS must be routed through the Sales accelerator work list
Conversational intelligence must be enabled for SMS analysis
explanation: An SMS is a contact from the organisation and carries consent and record-keeping obligations. Logging it on the timeline keeps the customer record complete like any other activity.

question: A maker proposes embedding a canvas app into an opportunity form to replace three fields with a custom layout. What should you weigh against it?
options: It becomes a second application to maintain, license, and secure
Canvas apps cannot read Dataverse from inside a model-driven form
Embedding a canvas app disables the form's business rules
Canvas apps cannot be included in a solution
explanation: Embedding is powerful and easy to overuse. A canvas app inside a form must earn its place against configuring the form properly, because it carries its own lifecycle cost.

question: A Power BI report embedded in a Sales dashboard shows a seller aggregate figures they cannot query in Dynamics. Why?
options: Power BI applies its own security model rather than Dataverse row-level security
Embedded reports run as the dashboard's owner by design
Dataverse row-level security does not apply to aggregate queries
The report is reading a cached export rather than live data
explanation: The two security boundaries are different, which is sometimes exactly what is wanted and sometimes a disclosure nobody intended. It is worth deciding which before embedding.

question: A cloud flow updating an opportunity is triggered by changes to that same opportunity and runs thousands of times a day. What should you configure?
options: A select-columns filter and a trigger condition on the trigger
A Condition as the flow's first action
A lower concurrency setting on the flow
A Terminate action at the end of the flow
explanation: Trigger-side filters are evaluated before a run starts, so the flow's own write never fires it. Anything inside the flow has already consumed the run.

question: Put these extension options in the order you should evaluate them for a Sales requirement.
items: Configure the standard form, view, or business rule
Add a Power Automate flow for the automation
Embed a Power Apps component or custom control
Build a pro-code extension outside the platform
explanation: Sales sits on Power Platform, so it follows the same ladder: configuration, then declarative automation, then embedded components, then pro-code. Each rung adds lifecycle cost.

question: Match each supporting capability to what it provides.

pairs.definition: Preparation, notes, and quick updates around a meeting
Calling from a record so the call is logged against it
Text as a tracked inbound and outbound path with consent
Analysis across volume and systems, under its own security

explanation: The first three extend where and how a seller works; the last extends what can be analysed, and is the only one that brings a different security boundary with it.
